newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Police have complained that a legal technicality is blocking their attempts to act against figures who helped Li Yung-chung, the suspected heroin trafficker, escape to Burma. Police sources say they have been frustrated because an investigation can be authorised only when a formal complaint is lodged by the judiciary, the damaged party in the Li affair. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- The Confederation of Thai Journalists has come out against a charter proposal which would prevent the government from shutting down publications and broadcasts "except by court order". The confederation has met and pinpointed the phrase "except by court order" of the charter draft. Critics have speculated that court-ordered shutdowns of publications and blackouts of radio and television broadcasts could still come without a trial. (THE NATION)

- Rakesh Saxena is expected to return to fight swindling charges soon after a Canadian court considers a request for his extradition, says acting commander of the Economic Crime Investigation Division. He says the proceedings will be dealt with in June and the former treasury adviser to Bangkok Bank of Commerce is expected to return shortly afterwards. (BANGKOK POST)

- The planned merger between Thai Danu Bank and Finance One Plc may have to be scrapped as the bank's shareholders are not satisfied with Finance One's financial status. Informed sources say the Bank of Thailand may have to resort to its "second" option of setting the stage to invite foreign firms to take over Finance One should Thai Danu Bank eventually walk out of the merger negotiations. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- Net applications for direct investment submitted by Thai and foreign investors to the Board of Investment in the first quarter fell by 22.3 percent from the same period last year. The sharp drop came amid a decline in Thailand's macro-economic stability which is being threatened by problems in the finance and property sectors. (THE NATION)

- Eastern Power is in danger of losing the right to sell electricity to the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT) in the first round of bidding because EGAT may transfer the bidding to the second round if an agreement is not reached. The issue involves a 300-megawatt electricity purchasing agreement under the Independent Power Producer program. (BUSINESS DAY)
